B051-03.notes: g(0) = f(0) - 2 = 3, so (0,3). Distractors model horizontal-shift and wrong-direction confusion.

B051-05.notes: Legs 6 and 6√3; area = (1/2)(6)(6√3) = 18√3. Distractor 36√3 forgets the 1/2.

flags: minor: 13 is odd and 18 is clearly too large (18^2 = 324 leaves 16, not consecutive), so back-solving from the choices takes only seconds; a typical student will get this as easily as an easy item
B051-06.notes: 12^2 + 14^2 = 144 + 196 = 340, so the larger is 14. Choice A (12) catches students who give the smaller integer.

B051-07.notes: 6 distinct arrangements: AABB, ABAB, ABBA, BAAB, BABA, BBAA; 2 begin with a pair (AABB, BBAA), so 1/3. Same result by drawing letters: the second letter matches the first with probability 1/3. Traps: 1/2 (treating each letter as independent) and 1/6 (counting only AABB).
